Neha/Karthik — draft answers below (technical details first, then suggested plain-language reply for Terrabay). Please flag anything that needs legal or infra edits.

1) Regions and pinning- Primary runtime for tenant request/response data is allocated in the region selected at tenant creation. For customers on the self-serve hosted tier, default is our US multi-zone pool (primary: us-east1). We offer an EU region (europe-west1) and APAC region (asia-southeast1) as paid add-ons. Enterprise customers may request a single-region "region-lock" during onboarding; this prevents automatic cross-region failover for data storage.

2) Retention windows (hosted API)- Conversation payloads (raw request and model response): retained for 45 days by default. This window is used to power observability, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
- Metadata & telemetry (request IDs, routing metadata, tokens consumed, error traces): retained for 365 days to support debugging and SLA investigations.
- Aggregated metrics and anonymized usage summaries: retained indefinitely for product analytics (customer-identifiable fields are removed).

3) Deletion / erasure process- Self-service erasure: customers can delete tenant data via the Console or API. Upon a deletion request we mark primary records for deletion and trigger an erase job.- Primary deletion SLA: majority of primary datastore records are removed within 72 hours of request (typical: 24–48 hours).- Backups & snapshots: we maintain incremental backups for disaster recovery; backups are retained up to 90 days. Backups are immutable in the short term; scheduled backup pruning removes data older than 90 days. Following a deletion request, backup restoration windows may require up to 14 days for deletion from all snapshot copies (this is our conservative operational bound).- Verification & audit: after erasure we provide a confirmation token and an audit record (timestamp, job id).

4) Legal hold / regulatory preservation- If a customer notifies Redwood of a legal hold, we suspend automated purge jobs for affected tenant identifiers and preserve relevant data until the hold is released. Holds are recorded in the audit trail; customers must provide legal request identifiers.

5) Encryption & access controls- All data at rest is encrypted with customer-tenant keys managed by Redwood KMS. Data in transit uses TLS 1.2+. Access to production data stores is restricted to a small SRE on-call group via role-based access and recorded by session logs.

6) Evidence and artifacts- SOC 2 CC documentation excerpt: soc2-data-handling-excerpt.txt (attached).
- Retention matrix and process diagram: see Redwood_HostedAPI_Data_Residency_Retention_Response_20261030.pdf (attached).

Suggested plain-language response to Terrabay (short):
We store hosted API customer data in the region chosen at onboarding (US by default). Conversation data is retained for 45 days; metadata is retained up to 365 days. Customers may request region-locking as an enterprise option. Deletion requests typically remove primary records within 72 hours and are propagated to backups within an operational bound of 14 days; we provide an audit token upon completion. We will pause automated purges if you notify us of a legal hold. Please see the attached PDF and SOC2 excerpt for evidence.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Michael —

Thanks for sending the questionnaire. Below are our consolidated answers for your compliance packet; I’ve attached a short evidence pack (retention matrix + SOC2 excerpt). If you need a signed attestation or additional logs for an audit, let me know and we’ll route through your account team.

Summary (concise):
- Region: Tenant data is stored in the region selected at onboarding. Default for self-serve is US (us-east1). EU and APAC regions are available as paid options; enterprise customers can request region-locking.
- Retention: Conversation payloads (request + response) retained for 45 days by default. Metadata/telemetry retained for 365 days. Aggregated/anonymized metrics are kept for product analytics.
- Deletion SLA: Primary records removed within 72 hours (typical 24–48 hours). Backup/snapshot propagation for deletion is operationally bound to 14 days; incremental backups are retained for up to 90 days. We provide an audit confirmation token once erasure jobs complete.
- Legal hold: We will suspend automated purge processes when notified of a valid legal hold and record the hold in the audit trail.
- Security controls: Data encrypted at rest with tenant-keying via Redwood KMS; TLS for in-transit; RBAC and session-audited access for privileged operations.

Attachments: Redwood_HostedAPI_Data_Residency_Retention_Response_20261030.pdf (summary + retention matrix), soc2-data-handling-excerpt.txt (supporting SOC2 control excerpt), Terrabay_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (your completed sheet).
